title: Short-nose crank wobble
symptoms: rhythmic knocking or clacking from the front of the engine
keyway damage found during belt service
cause: 1990 to early 1991 engines use a crankshaft with a short snout. If the center bolt loosens, the keyway wallows out and the pulley wobbles.
fix: Inspect the pulley for wobble at idle. Catch it early: clean, use a new key, Loctite and correct torque. If the crank keyway is damaged, repairs range from a keyway weld/epoxy fix to a crank swap.

title: Cam angle sensor (CAS) O-ring leak
symptoms: oil on the back of the head near the firewall
cause: The CAS O-ring hardens and lets oil weep, which can soak the CAS connector.
fix: Mark the CAS position, remove it, replace the O-ring, reinstall in the same spot, then check timing.

title: Valve cover gasket and spark plug well leaks
fix: Replace the valve cover gasket and half-moon seals; torque the bolts lightly (inch-pounds). Clean the plug wells and check the plug wires.

title: Lifter (hydraulic lash adjuster) tick
symptoms: ticking from the top of the engine
cause: Varnish or wear in hydraulic lash adjusters, low or old oil.
fix: Change the oil and filter with a quality oil, check the oil level, drive normally. Replace the lifters only if a tick persists hot.

title: Rough or hunting idle
symptoms: stalls when coming to a stop
cause: Carbon in the ISC (BAC) valve, vacuum leaks (cracked hoses, intake boot), misadjusted TPS, or the base idle screw set wrong.
fix: Check codes 12 and 34. Smoke-test or spray-test for vacuum leaks, clean the ISC valve, check the TPS idle switch, then set base idle and timing with TEN grounded.

title: Cranks but will not start
cause: Common culprits: main relay or circuit opening (fuel pump) relay, failed fuel pump, ignition coil or igniter, CAS, or a corroded ground.
fix: Check for spark first, then fuel pressure. Jump the fuel pump test terminal (F/P to GND) in the diagnosis connector with the ignition on to hear if the pump runs. Inspect the main and fuel pump relays.

title: Clogged top drains and rocker rust
symptoms: rust bubbles on the rear of the rockers
cause: Soft-top drain tubes behind the seats clog and send water into the rocker panels.
fix: Clear both drains with trimmer line from the top. Inspect rockers and treat rust early.

title: Pop-up headlight motors
cause: Worn motor, corroded connector, or weak retract relay.
fix: Use the manual knob under the rubber cap to test, check the relay and connectors, then rebuild or replace the motor.

title: Clutch hydraulics
cause: Worn master or slave cylinder, or old fluid with air in the line.
fix: Bleed the clutch first; replace the slave and/or master if the pedal still sinks. Check the fluid level in the clutch reservoir.

title: Overheating
cause: Cracked plastic radiator tank, stuck thermostat, failing water pump (often after a timing belt job is skipped), air in the system, or a failed fan or fan switch.
fix: Stop driving if the gauge climbs past normal. Pressure-test, check that the fans come on, bleed the system using the bleed screw at the thermostat housing, and inspect the radiator tanks.
